outcome: Optimal D-dimer cut-off value for PE diagnosis
Risk factors for PE after cesarean section
cohort: 289 women who underwent diagnostic imaging for suspected acute PE after cesarean delivery
finding: A D-dimer cut-off value of 800 ng/mL provided high sensitivity (96.67%) and increased specificity (34.74%) for detecting PE after cesarean section, potentially reducing unnecessary CT scans.
mod_finding: This study suggests that using a higher D-dimer threshold can reduce the number of unnecessary CT scans and subsequent radiation exposure in women after a cesarean delivery.
